cells.value: Pay-per-request payments over HTTP 402
cells.detail: The server prices a request in a 402 response, the client signs a payment, a facilitator verifies and settles it.

cells.value: Settlement rails and payment credential; discovery through Bazaar; refunds in auth-capture, batch-settlement channels and Solana upto
cells.detail: No identity, intent or checkout layer. Only auth-capture refunds captured funds; the channel schemes return unused escrow.

cells.value: x402 Foundation (Linux Foundation); TSC: Coinbase, Cloudflare, Stripe
cells.detail: Originated at Coinbase Developer Platform.

cells.value: Foundation under an LF Projects technical charter
cells.detail: TSC with one vote per representative and majority decisions; 75 percent supermajority for Core Principles.

cells.value: Apache-2.0 for code; CC BY 4.0 for documentation under the technical charter
cells.detail: The repository has one Apache-2.0 LICENSE and no CC BY file, and the charter does not say whether specification files count as documentation. The charter (2026-03-31, section 9.b) also requires a Developer Certificate of Origin sign-off on inbound code; CONTRIBUTING.md requires signed commits (GPG, SSH or S/MIME).
Whitepaper and public launch; npm x402 0.3.0 was published the same day, after earlier releases from 2025-03-03.
V2 launched 2025-12-11.

cells.value: Live (V2 since 2025-12-11)
cells.detail: upto, batch-settlement and auth-capture are 2026 additions with uneven SDK coverage; the Lightning binding (2026-09-23) had no SDK implementation on 2026-10-19.

cells.value: HTTP headers, MCP _meta, A2A task metadata
cells.detail: Facilitator APIs are currently standardized as HTTP endpoints, whatever the transport.

cells.value: EVM chains, Solana, Lightning and other CAIP-2 networks; credit-backed cloudflare:402
cells.detail: Fiat ids such as ach:us appear only as examples of the id format.

cells.value: None in the core; optional extensions
cells.detail: sign-in-with-x (CAIP-122), auth-hints (OAuth 2.0 with DPoP), RFC 9421 agent signatures in cloudflare:402.

cells.value: The client signature on each payment
cells.detail: No user mandate object. The a2a-x402 embedded flow carries x402 inside AP2 v0.1 mandates (CartMandate), which AP2 v0.2 no longer has.

cells.value: Both
cells.detail: Built for unattended clients with SDK spend controls; @x402/paywall serves humans; AP2 ships human-present and human-not-present x402 samples.

cells.value: The resource server
cells.detail: In cloudflare:402 the network (Cloudflare) is merchant of record.

cells.value: Signed payment authorization
cells.detail: EIP-3009 or Permit2 signatures, ERC-7710 delegations, a partially signed Solana transaction, or a Lightning preimage.

cells.value: EIP-712 typed-data signatures; Ed25519 for RFC 9421 and Solana; SHA-256 preimages on Lightning
cells.detail: Smart wallets through ERC-1271 and ERC-6492.

cells.value: Single-use nonce plus a validity window, enforced by the token contract
cells.detail: Replay stores for Lightning payment hashes; cumulative vouchers in batch-settlement.

cells.value: None in the protocol; SDK default of $1 per payment
cells.detail: Budgets are out of scope in the spec; upto signs a ceiling.

cells.value: No revocation message in x402; the signer can cancel an unused EVM authorization on chain before settlement
cells.detail: EIP-3009 cancelAuthorization (Base USDC implements it), Permit2 nonce invalidation or revoking an ERC-7710 delegation, if it lands before the facilitator settles. auth-capture adds void and client reclaim; channels allow timed withdrawal.

cells.value: No refunds in exact; no dispute process
cells.detail: auth-capture refunds captured funds; batch-settlement channels and Solana upto return unused escrow; third-party x402r adds refunds and arbitration.

cells.value: On-chain settlements (EVM, Solana) are public; resource metadata reaches the facilitator
cells.detail: Payment payloads and settlement responses stay between client, server and facilitator. The 402 offer is visible to any requester and to discovery services; Lightning and cloudflare:402 payments do not appear on a public chain.

cells.value: Bazaar extension and GET /discovery/resources
cells.detail: Public CDP Bazaar; x402scan reads /openapi.json and /.well-known/x402.

cells.value: Permissionless
cells.detail: Anyone can run a facilitator; cloudflare:402 needs the signature agent registered with Cloudflare.

cells.value: Open and permissionless, concentrated in practice
cells.detail: In x402scan figures reported on 2026-07-21, Coinbase's facilitator carried about half of transactions and two thirds of volume. From 2025-09-17 to 2026-06-23 one facilitator held 63.54 percent of Base settlements and another 67.72 percent of Solana's.

cells.value: 3 of 5
cells.detail: Public settlements and endpoints, but payments look like ordinary transfers and payment payloads stay private.

cells.value: No protocol fee; facilitator fee plus gas
cells.detail: CDP: 1,000 free on-chain transactions a month, then $0.001 each; verification free (as of 2026-10-11). The facilitator pays gas on the EVM exact path and as Solana fee payer.

cells.value: Facilitator pays gas; seller pays the facilitator fee
cells.detail: On Solana the merchant can sponsor as fee payer; cloudflare:402 is billed by Cloudflare.

cells.value: HTTP 402, EIP-712, EIP-3009, Permit2, ERC-7710, CAIP-2, CAIP-122, RFC 9421, BOLT11
cells.detail: Plus ERC-8021 builder codes.

cells.value: AP2 (a2a-x402, AP2 v0.1 target), ERC-8004, Stripe MPP, Mastercard Agent Pay for Machines (builds on x402, 2026-10-20)
cells.detail: Visa TAP is a looser fit: its browsingIOU answers an HTTP 402 with card-settlement fields, not the x402 format, and Visa's sample merchant names its flow x402. The ACP and UCP repositories do not mention x402 (searched 2026-10-19).

cells.value: @x402 TypeScript 2.28.0, PyPI x402 2.25.0, Go module v2 (versions on 2026-10-19)
cells.detail: Java is in the repository but unpublished. The legacy V1 npm package x402 still had 1.91M downloads in the 30 days to 2026-10-16.

cells.value: Real but contested
cells.detail: x402.org has shown the same Last 30 days figures (75.41M transactions, $24.24M) since at least 2025-12-14, with no update date; x402scan counted $1.23M in the 30 days to 2026-10-19. Visa and Artemis adjusted cumulative activity to about $15.0M across 109.6M transactions (data to 2026-04-21).

cells.value: Yes: six 2026 papers and two high-severity advisories (no CVE ids on 2026-10-19)
cells.detail: Five attacks, free-riding flaws, facilitator risks, A402, PII leakage, formal analysis; GHSA-3j63-5h8p-gf7c and GHSA-qr2g-p6q7-w82m.

cells.value: Stablecoin rules fall mainly on issuers; whether a non-custodial facilitator is a money transmitter is unsettled; sanctions duties apply to every US person
cells.detail: No KYC or sanctions layer in the protocol; the CDP facilitator runs OFAC and KYT checks.

cells.value: How much activity is real commerce, and can payment and delivery be made atomic?

radar.justification: Apache-2.0 code and CC BY 4.0 documentation (technical charter) in a public repository, governed by a Linux Foundation project; anyone can implement or run a facilitator.
Permissionless facilitation and many networks, but one facilitator carries most volume and three companies form the TSC.
V2 live since 2025-12-11 with frequent SDK releases and three contract audits; several schemes are 2026 additions.
Measurable on-chain activity and live products, but volume figures are contested and partly manufactured.
Designed for unattended clients that pay per request with SDK spend controls; no user mandate object of its own.
No dispute process and no refund in exact; auth-capture adds refunds and reclaim, and the channel schemes return unused escrow.

controlsCells.note: Identity is optional and separate from payment: sign-in-with-x (CAIP-122 wallet proof), auth-hints (OAuth 2.0 with DPoP) and RFC 9421 agent signatures in cloudflare:402.
No registry in x402. ERC-8004 can record that an agent accepts x402; cloudflare:402 needs the signature agent registered with Cloudflare.
The protocol has no consent object. The browser paywall asks a human in the UI; agents rely on mandates from other protocols such as AP2.
Budgets are out of scope in the spec. The TypeScript client applies spendControls by default (default assets only, $1 per payment); upto signs a ceiling.
With EIP-3009 and Permit2 the client's signature covers payTo and the amount; with ERC-7710 the delegation's caveats must. EVM upto also names the one facilitator allowed to settle.

validAfter, validBefore, the Permit2 deadline, maxTimeoutSeconds and Lightning invoice expiry bound exact, upto, auth-capture and Lightning authorizations. Batch-settlement vouchers carry no expiry and stay claimable until the escrow is drained; ERC-7710 delegations carry whatever limits the delegator set.

x402 has no revocation message. The signer can race the facilitator by canceling an unused EVM authorization on chain before settlement: EIP-3009 cancelAuthorization (Base USDC implements it), Permit2 nonce invalidation or revoking an ERC-7710 delegation. auth-capture adds void and client reclaim after the capture deadline; batch-settlement channels allow timed withdrawal.

The core specification defines no step-up to the human. The auth-hints extension lets a server require OAuth authentication for specific payment options (a 401 challenge), which identifies the client but is not a risk-based escalation.
Single-use 32-byte nonces enforced by EIP-3009 tokens, Permit2 nonces, cumulative vouchers, and replay stores for Lightning payment hashes.
PAYMENT-RESPONSE carries the transaction hash; the optional offer-receipt extension signs offers and receipts (TypeScript only).

No dispute or chargeback process. exact defines no refund; auth-capture adds void, refund and reclaim, batch-settlement channels refund unclaimed escrow, Solana upto returns unused escrow, and third parties such as x402r add arbitration.
None in x402. ERC-8004 feedback can carry proofOfPayment for an x402 payment.

On-chain settlements (EVM, Solana) are public but look like ordinary transfers; /supported, Bazaar and x402scan expose endpoints and 402 offers. Payment payloads, Lightning payments and cloudflare:402 commitments are not public.
No protocol kill switch. Clients stop by policy or spendControls; servers stop by removing routes; facilitators can refuse to settle.
